answer: Reputation-Weighted Work Spiral. Each identity’s task allocation follows a spiral: new agents get small jobs, and job value grows only after completed work is confirmed by unrelated peers. A clone starts at the spiral’s base, so an attacker must fund and operate every duplicate through the same slow ramp. A jetty rule caps concurrent jobs per identity, forcing clones to idle. An anchor score ties payout to verified history, so fresh clones earn near zero despite real compute cost.
